title: Demand Expansion and Cannibalization Effects from Retail Store Entry: A Structural Analysis of Multichannel Demand
authors: Scott K. Shriver; Bryan K. Bollinger
eligible_reason: No binary staggered treatment. Identification uses within-customer variation in distance to the nearest retail store generated by staggered store entries, but the treatment is continuous distance (dist / store_mindist) or distance bins (i.dbin), estimated with xtpoisson/xtreg customer fixed effects, quarter dummies and CSA-specific linear trends (i.csa_newid#c.t) in the descriptive section, and then a Bayesian hierarchical structural demand model (MATLAB MCMC). Continuous/multi-valued treatment, Poisson models and unit-group trends are all excluded.
design_notes: data_descriptives.do: xtpoisson trip i.dbin i.t i.csa_newid#c.t, fe; xtreg exptot i.dbin i.t i.csa_newid#c.t, fe robust (Section 3 descriptives). main.m / exhibits.m: structural model and counterfactuals (Tables 5-13).
estimators_reported: xtpoisson FE with distance bins and CSA trends (descriptive)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Store entries are staggered but treatment is continuous distance, not a binary adoption indicator.
data_files: wcai_data.csv (37 MB; outcomes SIMULATED from structural estimates per NDA)
data/census_blocks.dta, demogs_bg.dta, tax_rates.dta, tract2csa.dta, tract2zip.csv, fips2state.csv, online_tax_states.dta (public auxiliary inputs)
data_files_note: README: WCAI transaction data under NDA; the shipped wcai_data.csv is 'a synthetic data set' with model-simulated outcomes; exhibits 'will differ slightly' from the paper.
software_notes: MATLAB (structural estimation, MCMC) and Stata (prep_data.do, data_descriptives.do).
priority_note: Not a DiD design; synthetic outcomes.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). README extracted from the archive zip to the scratchpad.
